title: Finite semilinear exchange: pasting and quotient-coefficient naturality
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $g:Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be an isomorphism of underlying schemes, with Cartesian pullback $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]; $g,g'$ need not be $k$-linear. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY)$ and its base change $c'=(j',p')$, with induced isomorphism $\bar g:\overline X'\to\overline X$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use finite coefficients $A_n$, the pro-etale categories and the specified mate-followed-by-open exchange $e_f^c=\operatorname{Ex}_!^c$ of [def-exchange-projection]. Then these actual transformations satisfy the following equations, with canonical pullback, direct-image and open-extension compositors inserted.

For the identity isomorphism $e_1^c=1$. For a second underlying-scheme isomorphism $h:Y''\to Y'$ with induced $h':X''\to X'$, and the successively pulled-back compactification, the horizontal equation is
$$e_{gh}^c=(e_h^{c'}G_{g'})\circ(G_he_g^c),\qquad G_u=u^{-1}.$$
For vertical composition let $h_0:Y\to Z$ be another separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $u:Z'\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$ an underlying-scheme isomorphism inducing the square for $f$, and choose a compatible tower of compactifications of $f,h_0,h_0f$ [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. Let $F_v=Rp_{v,*}j_{v,!}$ denote the compact-support candidate for each chosen compactification, with primes denoting base change. Let $D:F_{h_0}F_f\to F_{h_0f}$ be its canonical proper/open composition comparison, formed from the normalized proper/open interchange [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], and $D'$ its base change. Then
$$e_{h_0f}(G_uD)=(D'G_{g'})(F_{h_0}'e_f)(e_{h_0}F_f).$$
This is an equality of the constituent transformations wherever they are defined; on bounded-below etale-origin inputs carrying the witnesses of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], $D,D'$ are the canonical isomorphisms of [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-composition-pasting-coherence], evaluated on constant strict towers.

For every quotient $A_n\to A_m$ with $1\leq m\leq n$, $e_f^c$ commutes with derived coefficient extension $-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$ on finite constructible finite-Tor inputs [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], under the pullback and compact-support coefficient comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. This equality includes the proper-factor square with its counit-defined projection map and the open-factor square with its unit-normalized coefficient comparison; it does not assert invertibility of a projection map for an arbitrary ordinary direct image. No $k$-linearity of $u,g,h$ is required.

proof.text: For the identity square, identify the exact derived pullback unit pullId with the localization of the module identity comparator. The left and right module compositor unit laws descend to the derived category. Cancel their invertible factors to identify ordinarySquare with the unit square. Transpose under the ordinary proper adjunction and apply mateEquiv_counit to obtain the identity formula for ordinaryE. For ordinaryBeta, transpose its inverse under the exact open adjunction, use ordinaryBetaInv_unit and the same square identity, and use naturality of the open unit. Cancel beta inverse and then the mapped pullId to assemble the identity formula for ordinaryH. These are the unit-normalized operations of [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization], [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] and [lem-pur-relative-compact-support-pasting].

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-relative-compact-support-pasting] in its ordinary constant-$B$ setting, with $B=A_n$, $a=g$, $b=h$, and the successively pulled-back compactifications. Its $E,\beta,H$ are exactly the $E,\beta,e^c$ of Step 1 (over $S=Y$ all the maps in question are $S$-maps). Its equality $H_{a\circ b}=(H_bA_{a_X})\circ(A_bH_a)$ therefore reads $e_{gh}^c=(e_h^{c'}G_{g'})\circ(G_he_g^c)$. The projection-preserving fibre-product identifications in that lemma are the compositors stipulated here.

source.place: Tag 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal), applied to the existing compactification-relative pasting lemma

proof.text: For the supplied compatible tower write $X\xrightarrow cU\xrightarrow b\bar X\xrightarrow p\bar Y\xrightarrow qZ$, with $i:Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y$ and $p_Y:U\to Y$, as in [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-composition-pasting-coherence]. Put $B=A_n$. In the strict-tower categories the base-change identity of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] for $Q=(b,i,p_Y,p)$ commutes the proper/open mate $\gamma_Q$ with its base change. Whisker that identity on the left by the base-changed $R_q$ and on the right by $J_c$. Replace the consecutive proper exchanges by the exchange for their composite using clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], and the consecutive open comparisons by that for $bc$ using [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization]. With $D=R_q\gamma_QJ_c$ and $F_f=R_{p_Y}J_c$, $F_{h_0}=R_qJ_i$, $F_{h_0f}=R_{qp}J_{bc}$ this gives exactly the displayed vertical equation, as an equality of transformations before evaluation. Evaluate on the constant tower of any finite-coefficient input. By [lem-cbc-tower-mate-evaluation-scalars], evaluation preserves inverse image, open extension, direct image, units, counits and mates; the open maps evaluate to the specified finite maps by the beta-normalization lemma. Consequently this is the required ordinary finite transformation identity. This proves the vertical transformation identity; invertibility on retained finite origins is treated separately below.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), compatible-tower construction; existing strict-tower vertical interchange followed by evaluation

proof.text: For compositionIsIso put B=A_n with its discrete topology. The unique underlying-additive-sheaf comparison identifies etaleOriginRealization with C_B of [def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport]; exact localization and the retained witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] identify the input with HD of its bounded-below etale antecedent. Apply the etale open extension along the first compactification open immersion to this antecedent. The normalized hJ comparison identifies its HD realization with the actual ordinary open extension of the input. Apply [lem-cbc-single-level-finite-proper-open-transport] to the central proper/open square. Both hR maps, both hJ maps, and the etale normalizedComparison are invertible; cancel the first two factors to deduce invertibility of the central singleDerivedGamma. Naturality transfers this to the identified input. The other factors of composition are open and proper compositors and equality transports, hence isomorphisms. Their composite is therefore invertible. This argument also works for every retained witness after base change and uses no tower evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), central proper/open interchange on a bounded-below finite etale antecedent.

proof.text: Identify scalarPull with the inverse scalar-adjunction mate proEtaleReductionPullbackInv of the canonical restriction/pullback square of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners]. The iterated-mate identity and [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] identify its conjugate with the specified proper-image restriction map; uniqueness of left adjoints proves the identification. Apply [lem-sp-scalar-tensor-pullback-square] to the actual quotient of the small coefficient rings and its ULift. Compose its inverse-square equation with the target square isomorphism to obtain the forward pull-comparison cube. The first conjunct of [lem-fix-basic-operation-coefficient-coherence] is coefficientOperationMateEquations, universally quantified over coefficient changes and scheme morphisms; specialize its auxiliary schemes to the empty scheme and its coefficient field to the given finite extension. Its counit equations identify the actual properComparison maps with the prescribed proper projection mates. The exchanges ordinaryE have the mateEquiv_counit equations by definition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coefficient-exchange-mates] to the four ordinary proper adjunctions and this cube. No proper coefficient comparison is inverted.

The actual openRestriction comparison is the inverse of scalarJ from [lem-cbc-tower-mate-evaluation-scalars]: expand both definitions and use preservation of inverse natural isomorphisms under exact descent. The theorem scalar_open_normalized supplies its open-unit equation. Transpose this equation across the two scalar adjunctions, using the defining inverse-mate unit equations for scalarPull and openComparison. Naturality of the units and the scalar restriction/pullback square, followed by cancellation of its inverse, gives the open-unit equation for the inverse of openComparison. The inverse geometric open exchanges satisfy ordinaryBetaInv_unit from [lem-pur-relative-compact-support-pasting]. Rotate the same concrete scalar/pullback cube used for properCoefficient by cancelling invertible square and pullback comparisons. Apply [lem-pur-open-scalar-exchange-unit-mates] to the four exact ordinary open adjunctions with these specified unit equations. Both three-factor composites are invertible; equality of their inverses gives exactly the displayed forward open coefficient square. No constructibility or flatness restriction is used in this constituent identity.

proof.text:
The chosen-compactification coefficient comparison is
$$\kappa_f^c=(P_p^m\delta_j)(\rho_pJ_j^n):T_Y(P_p^nJ_j^n)\longrightarrow P_p^mJ_j^mT_X.$$
These are the proper projection and open tensor comparisons: [lem-fix-operation-reduction] supplies the compact-support comparison on the stated constructible finite-Tor domain and says it preserves the tensor maps, units and counits specifying these factors. Substitute $e_g^a=(P_{p'}^a\beta_g^a)(E_g^aJ_j^a)$ into both routes of the desired coefficient square. First use Step 4 at $J_j^nK$, then naturality of $\rho_{p'}$ with respect to $\beta_g^n$, and then Step 5. Associating these composites gives
$$ (F_{f'}^m\chi_{g'})(\kappa_{f'}^{c'}G_{g'}^n)(T_{Y'}e_g^n)=(e_g^mT_X)(G_g^m\kappa_f^c)(\chi_gF_f^n),$$
This is exactly commutation with quotient extension under the stipulated comparisons. All transformations used are on underlying ringed pro-etale topoi; their hypotheses impose no $k$-linearity on the isomorphisms.
